evidence.paraphrase: The page motivates a PCE inflation measure that reduces the influence of unusually large positive and negative component price changes each month.
Component price changes are sorted and the weighted lower twenty-four percent and upper thirty-one percent of the distribution are removed before averaging.
The remaining component price changes are averaged with PCE expenditure weights, preserving a transparent contribution calculation for the retained mass.
The asymmetric trim fractions were selected from historical fit to proxies for underlying inflation, which creates a tuning choice that requires stability and out-of-sample checks.

executive_summary: The Dallas Fed trimmed-mean PCE measure is a transparent cross-sectional transform: order monthly PCE component price changes, remove expenditure-weighted tails, and average the remaining mass. The specific lower twenty-four and upper thirty-one percent trims were chosen historically to track underlying inflation, so MacroTrace must preserve component weights, boundary handling, add-up checks, and out-of-sample sensitivity rather than treating the tuning constants as universal truth.

method_routes.aggregation_role: deterministic factor transform feeding underlying-inflation nodes; no learned cross-lane weight
method_routes.estimand: monthly underlying PCE price change after removing registered expenditure-weighted tail mass
method_routes.formula: sort component inflation pi_j; trim cumulative weight below 24 percent and above 69 percent; TRIM=sum retained w_j pi_j/sum retained w_j
method_routes.identification_strategy: deterministic robust aggregation rather than causal estimation
identifying_assumptions: component prices and expenditures share the same PCE vintage
weights add to the registered aggregate
robustness_requirements: median PCE and core PCE benchmarks
method_routes.sample_definition: complete detailed monthly PCE component table for each data vintage
